title: Conservation of Mass and Balanced Equations Practice
description: Practice using mass conservation and atom counts to explain why chemical equations must balance.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the Law of Conservation of Mass?
options: Matter is created whenever a new substance forms.
Matter is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.
Products always have less mass than reactants.
Atoms disappear when they become gases.
questions.explanation: The law says matter is not created or destroyed. Atoms are rearranged, so total mass is conserved in a closed system.

questions.question: In a closed container, 6 g of hydrogen reacts with 48 g of oxygen. What total mass of product forms?
questions.explanation: Add the reactant masses: 6 g + 48 g = 54 g. In a closed system, product mass equals total reactant mass.

questions.question: A balanced chemical equation has the same number of each kind of atom on both sides of the arrow.
questions.explanation: Balanced equations show conservation of atoms by matching each element's atom count on the reactant and product sides.

questions.question: Which equation shows the formation of water as a balanced equation?
questions.explanation: In 2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O, both sides have 4 H atoms and 2 O atoms.

questions.question: Fill in the missing mass: 12 g of carbon reacts with 32 g of oxygen to form ____ g of carbon dioxide.
questions.explanation: The total reactant mass is 12 g + 32 g = 44 g, so 44 g of product forms in a closed system.

questions.question: For the equation N2 + 3H2 -> 2NH3, how many hydrogen atoms are on the reactant side?
questions.explanation: The coefficient 3 means three H2 molecules. Each H2 has 2 H atoms, so 3 x 2 = 6 hydrogen atoms.

questions.question: Changing H2O to H2O2 is a valid way to balance an equation for making water.
questions.explanation: Changing a subscript changes the substance. H2O is water, while H2O2 is hydrogen peroxide.

questions.question: In one or two sentences, explain why chemical equations must be balanced.
questions.correctAnswer: Chemical equations must be balanced because atoms are not created or destroyed in a chemical reaction. The same number of each kind of atom must appear on the reactant and product sides.
questions.explanation: A balanced equation is the symbolic way to show conservation of mass and conservation of atoms.
